about.what: Headline levels and daily moves for the main US equity indexes, volatility, the dollar, rates, gold, oil and bitcoin.
about.why: A 10-second read of today's risk tone across asset classes.
about.how_to_read: Stocks up, VIX down and credit calm is risk-on. A rising dollar and yields with falling equities is a tightening-financial-conditions day. Gold up alongside a falling dollar often reflects easing expectations.

about.what: Total returns of the 11 GICS sectors of the S&P 500, using the SPDR Select Sector ETFs.
about.why: Sector leadership shows what the market is pricing about the cycle. Cyclicals lead in early or mid expansions, defensives lead in slowdowns.
about.how_to_read: Tech, Discretionary, Financials and Industrials leading is risk-on or growth-optimistic. Utilities, Staples and Health Care leading is defensive or late-cycle. Energy and Materials leading often coincides with inflationary periods.

about.what: Total returns of bond ETFs across the Treasury curve, credit quality and international markets. Each row also shows trailing-12-month distribution yield and approximate effective duration.
about.why: Bonds show the macro story through two levers. Duration measures sensitivity to interest rates. Spread measures sensitivity to credit risk and growth.
about.how_to_read: Long Treasuries (TLT) outperforming short ones is a bet on falling rates or growth fears. High-yield outperforming Treasuries is risk-on. Duration ≈ % price change for a 1pp rate move (TLT with ~16y duration loses ~16% if long yields rise 1pp). Yields are trailing distribution yields, not yield-to-maturity.

about.what: Returns of front-month commodity futures across energy, metals and agriculture, plus broad commodity index ETFs.
about.why: Commodities are the purest read on real-economy demand (copper, oil), inflation pressure and supply shocks (weather, geopolitics).
about.how_to_read: Copper and oil rising together is a pro-growth, reflationary signal. Gold rising while copper falls is defensive or a monetary hedge. Front-month continuous futures include roll effects, so long-horizon returns differ from what a futures investor actually earned.

about.what: Performance of major and emerging-market currencies against the US dollar (positive = the currency strengthened vs USD), plus the Dollar Index and bitcoin.
about.why: The dollar is the world's funding currency. A strong dollar tightens global financial conditions, pressures EM and commodities, and dents US multinational earnings.
about.how_to_read: Broad USD weakness is usually risk-on and good for EM and commodities. JPY and CHF strength often signals risk-off (safe-haven flows, carry unwinds). Differences in rates between countries drive most medium-term FX trends.
